paper.title: Coding session replay
paper.one_liner: Recorded coding events reveal how students work.

direction.title: Stuck Moment Detector
direction.what_you_would_make: Build a tool that identifies stuck/looping moments in real student coding sessions.
direction.first_visible_result: A coding session replay highlights possible stuck moments.

asset.title: TutorTrace coding event logs
asset.description: Real timestamped edit and run events, grouped by session. The reader has never used these logs.

rubric: First: Bart selects and shows one real coding session/example; the human is not asked to browse or choose it, and a detector is not required yet.
Second: one stuck behavior/default rule is demonstrated on that same example.
Third: the user controls one rule parameter/threshold and immediately sees the changed highlights on that example.
No initial multi-rule comparison system, cross-student dashboard, clustering/grouping, or aggregate cohort analytics.

paper.title: Cell image measurements
paper.one_liner: Microscope images show how cell shapes vary.

direction.title: Cell Shape Explorer
direction.what_you_would_make: Build a tool to investigate how a cell segmentation threshold changes measured cell area.

asset.title: Microscopy image collection
asset.description: Real microscopy images; the reader has never seen the images or performed segmentation.

rubric: First: Bart selects one real image or small subset and makes it inspectable before asking the reader to choose analyses.
Second: show one meaningful segmentation/measurement result using an agent-chosen default on that same image/subset.
Third: alter one meaningful threshold/variable and show the changed result on that same artifact.
No prerequisite study, user-selected analysis plan, general image-processing pipeline, or collection-wide analytics.

paper.title: Plain text editing
paper.one_liner: A small editor turns plain text into formatted notes.

direction.title: Markdown Note Preview
direction.what_you_would_make: Build a local note editor where users can see how their Markdown becomes formatted text.

asset.title: Existing local editor code
asset.description: An existing runnable editor repository with a sample note; no external dataset is needed.

rubric: First: make a concrete part of the existing editor visible/runnable with an agent-selected sample note.
Second: make one representative Markdown-to-preview workflow work on that same note.
Third: let the user change/test one meaningful formatting behavior and see the result on that same example.
No fabricated dataset dependency, prerequisite codebase study, general plugin framework, sync system, or full product feature milestones.
